subject: regionCounts returns different results in version 0.9.2 than 0.5.7

messages.author: 1648576ac1e3af20
messages.subject: regionCounts returns different results in version 0.9.2 than 0.5.7
parts:
Dear Altuna,
The regionCounts function is returning different values for numCs and numTs in version 0.9.2 than 0.5.7. The numC counts decrease and numT counts increase. Both samples are affected. The coverage columns are virtually identical between 0.9.2 and 0.5.6.

Input are the exact same files, subjected to exact same pipeline / commands. See attached scripts (unrelated commands have been removed). All features subjected to regionCounts show the same behavior.
I will use CpG island counts as an example. I have verified my CpG island features are non-overlapping. Run 1 was performed with 0.5.7. Run 2 was performed with 0.9.2. The first 100 lines of counts in both runs' methylbase objects are found in the attached zip file.

The following are counts for the first CpG island interrogated.
  • Counts in its run #1 methylBase object:
"chr1.3521706.3521924.chr1.3521705" "chr1" 3521706 3521924 "+" 128 114 14 167 151 16
151 / 167 = ~ 90.4% methylation for Sample # 2
  • Counts in run #2 methylBase object:
"chr" "start" "end" "strand" "coverage1" "numCs1" "numTs1" "coverage2" "numCs2" "numTs2"
"chr1" 3521706 3521924 "+" 128 2 126 167 0 167
0 / 167 = 0% methylation for Sample # 2
  • Counts in input file:
When I filter the original input file by 5x coverage, the CpG counts for the above island in sample #2 are 212 / 234 = ~ 90.6% methylation. Basically in agreement with run #1. The raw file CpG site counts in the CpG island are found in the attached zip file.

Regards,
Ben

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: regionCounts returns different results in version 0.9.2 than 0.5.7
parts:
Hi Ben,
I tried to replicate the case by using the example data in the package. However, it seems that the new version returns the values correctly. Here is what I did:
library(methylKit)
library(GenomicRanges)
data(methylKit)
methylBase.obj

# calculate the regional counts for a window
# containing first two CpGs
regionCounts(methylBase.obj,GRanges("chr21",ranges=IRanges(10011830,10011842 )) )



So this could have something to do with BSMAP file format, could you send me the subset of a methylBase object that overlaps with a problematic CpG island?

I need the subset of base-pair resolution methylBase object that you fed into regionCounts() function, I just need the CpGs from one or two of the problematic CpG islands where counts from two versions are not concordant.  My guess would be that there are some non-numeric characters in the unfiltered (5X coverage filter I'm talking about) file, and when they are read-in they cause this problem. But i need the methylBase object to verify that and/or look for other problems. You can save the subset of the methylBase object with saveRDS() or save() functions.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: regionCounts returns different results in version 0.9.2 than 0.5.7
parts:
Altuna,
I may be a little confused about what you would like to receive. The object fed into regionCounts() is a methylRawList.
In my first post, two attached files included head.WIvsKI.run02.CpGi.methylbase.txt and head.WIvsKI.run01.CpGi.methylbase.txt. Produced by write.table , they contain the first hundred lines from the CpG island methylBase object produced by unite of the object produced by regionCounts in the two separate runs. Every CpG island region is not concordant between runs.

In my current post, the following two attached files [ produced by save(head(getData)) ] are the first 1000 lines of the methylRawList object for sample 1 (WI) and sample 2 (KI) in run02 (methylKit 0.9.2). They contain at least the first two mm9 CpG islands which were interrogated.
KI.norm.methylRaw.run02.head1klines.rData
WI.norm.methylRaw.run02.head1klines.rData
In my current post, the following two attached files contain (1) the first 110,000 lines of output from the bsmap python script, methratio.py and (2) the first 5,000 CpG sites parsed from file (1) by awk for sample 2, KI, in the pair-wise comparison.
KI.bsmap.methratio.py.out.head110klines.txt.gz
KI.bsmap.methratio.py.out.awk.CpG.head5klines.txt.gz

I have examined some selected regions of the input files by `cat -tev` and did not observe any changes in non-printing character patterns.
I can say the underlying issue occurs between runs on 0.9.2 versus 0.5.7 for the same input file when the read pipeline uses fraction=TRUE for counting C's (ratio in input) and a two decimal float for counting coverage (eff_CT_count). As I mentioned previously, the exact same read pipeline is used in these two versions.
Further, the underlying issue occurs for similar input files (python script's CT snp correction parameter now set to false) when the read pipeline uses fraction=FALSE for counting C's .. thus C comes from an integer (C_count in input) and coverage taken from integer (CT_count in input).

# header and first two lines of the bsmap methratio.py script output
chr pos strand context ratio eff_CT_count C_count CT_count rev_G_count rev_GA_count CI_lower CI_upper
chr1 3000331 - TAGAT 0.000 1.00 0 1 0 0 0.000 0.793
chr1 3000346 - CAGAA 0.000 1.00 0 1 0 0 0.000 0.793

Best,
Altuna

parts:
Altuna,
My bad on the methylRawList object(s). I did not realize I was producing a data.frame rather than the S4 object you were looking for. The methylKit documentation clearly explains this, a testament to your excellent work.

After trying numerous permutations, I isolated the underlying issue to the pipeline's "fraction" parameter at the read() step. Reading into methylKit the file created by our bsmap python script, methratio.py.
Essentially, if methylKit pipeline is called with fraction=TRUE, the C and T counts are correct. If fraction = FALSE, the C and T counts are incorrect. I replicated the results in both 0.5.7 and 0.9.2. You can see the discrepancy in the first methylRawList object that is created. The attached zip archive contains the input files and a script which invokes read() twice, fraction = T , then = F. The script takes about two seconds to run.

Regards,
Ben
On Wednesday, January 15, 2014 8:10:18 AM UTC-6, Altuna Akalin wrote:

Basically, I need the subset of the data and the script that goes with that data that shows the discrepancy. Let me know if it is not clear

Best,
Altuna

Hi Ben,
I tried the function with methylRawList as well, it seems to be working correct. It will take time to sift through this data and it is not the format I was looking for, so if you can send exactly what I need I will look into this. What I need is whatever you feed into regionCounts() , it could be methylRawList, methylRaw or methylBase format, the objects you sent are not methylKit objects. 

I also need a couple of locations (CpG islands) where you observed discrepancy between the old and new versions. You can subset the methylRaw  and methylBase objects with [] notation, so that only the subset that overlaps with problematic example regions contained in the file. Then you can save the methylKit objects with saveRDS or save.

Alternatively, if you think that the recent files you sent have enough information to replicate the problem. You can send me the script that takes those flat BSMAP ratio files and processes them and  demonstrates the problem.

Best,
Altuna
